Monitor closely for potential systemic corticosteroid effects when using budesonide, as it may alter the metabolism of other drugs through hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 pathways. 2. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of iloperidone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while iloperidone increases budesonide levels through the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Iloperidone, a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, can elevate plasma levels of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor for potential interactions. 4. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of imatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of imipramine via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance remains uncertain. 6. Budesonide and indapamide may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypokalemia, especially with strong glucocorticoid activity. Monitor closely. 7. Indinavir increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Budesonide and indomethacin may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Budesonide reduces the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids also heighten the risk of infection with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Budesonide decreases the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (cell-cultured, quadrivalent) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids increase infection risk with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Budesonide reduces the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (intranasal, quadrivalent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids elevate infection risk with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Budesonide decreases the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (recombinant, quadrivalent) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immune response to the vaccine may be diminished in immunocompromised individuals. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Budesonide reduces the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (trivalent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids increase infection risk with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Budesonide decreases the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (intranasal, trivalent) via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids elevate infection risk with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Budesonide reduces the effects of insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 16. Isoniazid increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while budesonide decreases isoniazid levels through an unknown mechanism. Monitor closely. 17. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of isradipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Istradefylline increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 19. Itraconazole significantly increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for corticosteroid excess. 20. Ivacaftor increases budesonide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ivosidenib decreases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for therapeutic loss. 22. Budesonide reduces the effects of the Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids increase infection risk with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Ketoconazole increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for corticosteroid excess. 24. Budesonide and ketoprofen may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Budesonide and ketorolac (including intranasal) may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Lansoprazole decreases budesonide effects by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. This applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Lapatinib increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while budesonide decreases lapatinib levels through the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Larotrectinib increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Lasmiditan increases budesonide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Letermovir increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Levo-ketoconazole increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for corticosteroid excess. 32. Lonafarnib increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and adjust doses accordingly. 33. Lopinavir increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Budesonide decreases lopinavir levels through the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Loratadine increases budesonide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, while budesonide decreases loratadine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Budesonide and lornoxicam may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of lumefantrine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while lumefantrine decreases budesonide levels through the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Budesonide reduces the effects of macimorelin by an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Allow sufficient washout time for drugs affecting growth hormone release before administering macimorelin. 38. Magnesium oxide decreases budesonide effects by increasing gastric pH, potentially causing premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. This applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Budesonide decreases maraviroc levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Marijuana increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Mavorixafor increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Budesonide reduces the effects of the measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids increase infection risk with live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 44. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Budesonide decreases mesalamine levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Budesonide and mesterolone may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing edema formation. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Budesonide decreases mestranol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Budesonide reduces metformin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Metronidazole increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Budesonide reduces metyrapone effects through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 58. Miconazole (vaginal) increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Budesonide decreases midazolam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely.
